MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 






We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 


Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.




To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.







Supportive on the job development to grow your career 












Various additional leave options 












Based at Monash Medical Centre in Clayton 















Help shape the future of healthcare at Monash Health and embark on a rewarding career where your dedication makes a difference in people's lives. 






This role involves performing routine diagnostic laboratory tests according to established protocols to support patient care within Monash Health Pathology services. The position works under the supervision of a Principal Scientist and contributes to accurate, timely pathology results. Key aspects include: 









Laboratory testing: Performing haematology analyses in line with established protocols 












Morphology expertise: Demonstrated experience in blood film morphology, including identification and reporting of abnormalities 












Quality & safety: Adhering to quality assurance, control procedures, and safety standards 












Equipment & processes: Maintaining instruments, handling specimens and escalating abnormal or unexpected results 












Teamwork & communication: Working collaboratively with laboratory teams and contributing to efficient service delivery 












Flexibility: Availability for casual rotating roster across haematology services 















About the Department - Program






Alfred Health and Monash Health have established a formal partnership to deliver a Shared Pathology Service as one of two pathology networks for metropolitan Melbourne. All roles in the Pathology Programs are working to develop the Partnership and ensure we continue to provide high quality care for the patients across the health services. 






Monash Health Pathology is an integral part of Monash Health. It is the largest public provider of Pathology services in the state and currently operates 6 laboratories. The largest of these is located at the Monash Medical Centre, Clayton, with additional laboratories located at the Dandenong, Moorabbin, Casey, Victorian Heart Hospital and Wonthaggi Hospitals. There are currently 18 collection locations based within the hospital sites and community settings. Services are provided to the Public and Private sectors, and other laboratory services. 












About the Role 






Join the Monash Health Pathology team as a Medical Scientist Grade 1 within Haematology. In this role, you will work under the guidance of the Principal Scientist and collaborate closely with the broader multidisciplinary laboratory team across the Central Laboratory. 









The role focuses on delivering high-quality diagnostic services including routine haematology testing, transfusion testing and blood product support, and blood film morphology assessment, ensuring accurate and timely results to support patient care. You will perform laboratory testing in accordance with established protocols, carry out quality control procedures, and maintain laboratory equipment and processes. 












The Medical Scientist is responsible for ensuring the quality and safety of results at the point of care, recognising and escalating abnormal findings and contributing to continuous quality improvement initiatives. 












This role requires the ability to work both independently and collaboratively, with strong analytical skills, attention to detail and effective communication. A commitment to professional development, flexibility to work rostered and after hours shifts, and the ability to manage a varied workload in a fast-paced environment are essential. 












Experience in blood film morphology is highly valued, supporting accurate interpretation and reporting within haematology services. 












The role is a 24-7 rotational position with shifts that include day, early, afternoon, evening, overnight and weekend shifts. Particiaption in the on call roster.















About You 






To be successful in this healthcare role, you will bring the following demonstrated skills, experience, and attributes: 









Bachelor of Biomedical Science (Medical Laboratory Science) or recognised equivalent is essential 












Demonstrated experience or strong interest in haematology laboratory testing, including routine analysis and workflows 












Demonstrated experience or strong interest in transfusion science, including testing and blood product support. 












Proven experience in blood film morphology and the ability to accurately identify and interpret abnormal findings (highly regarded) 












Sound knowledge of laboratory instrumentation, quality control, and quality assurance procedures 












Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organisational skills with high attention to detail 












Ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team 












Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to effectively liaise with staff at all levels 












Demonstrated ability to work efficiently under pressure and meet clinical turnaround times 












Commitment to maintaining professional standards, ongoing learning, and participating in quality improvement initiatives 















Why you will love working with us 






Ours is a connected team with strong shared values and an unwavering commitment to excellence. We are a highly skilled, collaborative, and welcoming team where the only limit in your career is you. Upon your appointment, we will provide you with:









A supportive and cohesive sub-team, working within a larger consumer relations team.

For nearly 25 years, APD Global has set the benchmark in delivering advanced, comprehensive, and specialised engineering solutions.

We have around 800 employees including our alliance contracting partners, across 15 strategically located offices in Australia (Perth, Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Adelaide, Darwin), New Zealand and Malaysia. We specialise in seamless integration across the Power Systems, Telecommunications, and Renewable Energy industries. Our expertise spans Power Systems Studies, Transmission Lines, Substations, Telecommunications, Protection, Control & Automation, Renewable Energy Connections, Mining, and Engineering, Protection Panel Design and Installation, 3D Design and Manufacturing as well as Construction/Management (EPC/M) services.

We have outstanding opportunity for a highly experienced ACCEPTANCE ENGINEER. We are looking for trustworthy individuals with integrity who will bring a positive can-do attitude to the position and to the team. Position available in Vic, Qld, WA, and NSW.

Role Overview
The Acceptance Engineer works under the direction of the Acceptance Lead to support the successful acceptance, handover, and integration of new and upgraded network assets into Telstra’s operational environment. The role is responsible for ensuring all documentation, as-built records, and asset data are accurate, compliant, and correctly uploaded into Telstra’s DBoR systems in accordance with program and governance requirements.

KEY RESPONSIBILITY

ACCEPTANCE & HANDOVER
Support the Acceptance Lead in managing the end-to-end acceptance process for Telstra network assets.
Review and validate construction completion packs, ensuring readiness for acceptance and operational handover.
Facilitate the smooth transition of assets from delivery teams into Telstra operational ownership.

DOCUMENTATION & AS-BUILTS
Ensure all project documentation, including as-built drawings, design updates, and asset data, is accurate, complete, and compliant.
Upload and validate as-built information within Telstra’s DBoR systems upon project completion.
Maintain document version control and ensure alignment between physical assets and system records.

DBoR SYSTEM MANAGEMENT
Create, update, and validate asset records using Telstra’s legacy and current DBoR platforms, including: IDEAL, CANRAD, Structure Builder, MITS, RODS, RFNSA, CADlink, Multiman, CRAMER, TPD, WHISPER, TCSS, NETMAPS, WidePlan, Widefeas, CMART, and TRAC.
Resolve data discrepancies and support data quality audits as required by the program.

STAKEHOLDER COORDINATION
Work closely with the Acceptance Lead, internal Telstra teams, delivery partners, and external contractors to coordinate acceptance activities.
Support issue resolution relating to site access, design compliance, documentation gaps, and system data conflicts.
Act as a key interface between construction, design, and operational teams during acceptance and handover.

COMPLIANCE & GOVERNANCE
Ensure all works comply with Telstra design guidelines, relevant Australian Standards, and WHS/safety requirements.
Support program governance by ensuring acceptance processes align with Telstra policies and audit requirements.
Assist with continuous improvement initiatives across acceptance and handover processes.

SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE/QUALIFICATIONS
Experience working in network acceptance, handover, or asset management roles within Telstra or similar telecommunications environments.
Strong working knowledge of Telstra DBoR systems and acceptance workflows.
Ability to interpret engineering designs, construction drawings, and as-built documentation.
Strong stakeholder management and coordination skills.
High attention to detail with a focus on data accuracy and compliance.

If you have the skills required for this role and you feel this is the job for you, then apply now!
Work Location: Melbourne, Vic
Salary: $80,000 per annum + Super

IT Systems Analyst
Full-time
Glow Health Care Australia Pty Ltd trading as Glow Health Care Australia
Parramatta, NSW
Salary: $80,000–$100,000 plus superannuation
About the Role
Glow Health Care Australia is seeking an experienced IT Systems Analyst to support and improve the technology systems used across our disability, aged care, home care, allied health and NDIS service operations.
In this role, you will work with managers, employees, external vendors and technology teams to identify business needs, analyse existing systems and implement practical technology solutions. You will help ensure our systems are secure, reliable, compliant and aligned with the organisation’s operational requirements.
Duties and Responsibilities
•	Analyse existing systems, applications and business processes to identify opportunities for improvement. 
•	Consult with stakeholders to gather and document functional and technical requirements. 
•	Translate business requirements into system designs and technical specifications. 
•	Prepare system workflows, process maps, data mappings and functional documentation. 
•	Recommend system enhancements, new applications and improvements to existing platforms. 
•	Coordinate the implementation and rollout of new systems and system upgrades. 
•	Develop and conduct system, integration and user acceptance testing. 
•	Investigate system defects and coordinate resolutions with vendors and development teams. 
•	Support the integration of third-party applications with internal systems and platforms. 
•	Monitor system interfaces and data flows to maintain accuracy and interoperability. 
•	Prepare user guides, technical procedures, training materials and system documentation. 
•	Provide Level 2 and Level 3 support for complex system-related issues. 
•	Assist with staff training and change-management activities during system implementations. 
•	Ensure systems comply with privacy, cybersecurity, data-governance and healthcare requirements. 
•	Conduct post-implementation reviews and recommend further system improvements. 
Skills and Qualifications
•	Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Information Systems or a related discipline. 
•	At least two to three years of relevant experience as a Systems Analyst, Business Systems Analyst or in a similar ICT position. 
•	Experience analysing, implementing and supporting organisational or enterprise systems. 
•	Strong knowledge of requirements gathering, process mapping and technical documentation. 
•	Experience with system integration, APIs, databases and data modelling. 
•	Experience conducting integration testing and user acceptance testing. 
•	Familiarity with SQL, Visio, Jira, Confluence or similar tools. 
•	Understanding of Agile, Waterfall or other software-development methodologies. 
•	Strong analytical, troubleshooting and problem-solving skills. 
•	Excellent written and verbal communication skills. 
•	Ability to communicate technical information clearly to non-technical stakeholders. 
•	Knowledge of information security, privacy and data-governance principles. 
•	Experience in healthcare, disability, aged care, community services or NDIS operations is desirable. 
•	ITIL, CBAP, PRINCE2 or similar certification would be advantageous. 
How to Apply
Please submit your résumé and a cover letter outlining your relevant qualifications and experience.
Glow Health Care Australia is an equal-opportunity employer. We welcome applications from suitably qualified candidates from all backgrounds.

This role involves regular work at heights (6-10 meter transmission structures) and in confined spaces. You must be comfortable working at heights, as this is an essential requirement of the position.    Your day-to-day responsibilities will include: 
 
 Installing, maintaining, and troubleshooting fibre optic and data communication systems 
 Conducting site surveys to assess and deliver tailored communication solutions 
 Reading and interpreting cable plans and technical drawings 
 Performing high-quality installations in line with industry standards 
 Working at heights and within confined spaces in a safe and controlled manner 
 Liaising with clients to understand requirements and deliver effective outcomes 
 Ensuring all work is completed safely, efficiently, and to specification 
 
  What you'll need to succeed     We are open-minded on background - the key focus for us is attitude, aptitude, and a genuine interest in data communications.   You'll ideally bring: 
 
 Experience in telecommunications, electrical, or data communications environments 
 Exposure to fibre optic installation, termination, or testing (highly regarded) 
 ACMA Open Cabling Registration (or willingness to obtain) 
 Current manual driver's licence 
 Ability to work autonomously and as part of a team 
 Strong problem-solving skills and a safety-first mindset 
 Flexibility to travel to remote sites (Monday-Friday) 
  Comfort and capability working at heights (essential)  
 A proactive attitude and willingness to learn and develop 
 
  Desirable but not essential:  
 
 Cert III in Telecommunications 
 MR Licence (or willingness to obtain - support provided) 
 Previous site-based experience in infrastructure, electrical, or comms projects 
 
  What you'll get in return     
 
 Stable, full-time employment with a strong project pipeline

 Flights, transport, and logistics provided for remote work   
 Ongoing training, mentoring, and career development pathways
